A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bongard-problem diagnostic study. Their main texts, figures, tables, and complete supplementary sections can be matched reliably despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of eight VLMs on 100 Bongard problems and a human study with 20 analyzed participants.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds an image-presentation control using GPT-4o and Claude.

M1.justification: The diagnostic framework, task definitions, models, and original prompts remain unchanged. The additional image-presentation experiment is a control within the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 100 high-resolution original Bongard problems, reasoning tasks, and human population. The new control repackages the same twelve diagrams within the existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The same eight VLMs and human comparison are retained. The new control uses already evaluated GPT-4o and Claude; standardized model names in the appendix do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: v4 Appendix B.4 adds a controlled presentation variant: twelve individual images replace the composite BP image, with corresponding adjustments to the prompt introduction. The original experiments' settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 and Table 14 add a focused test of whether composite-image presentation explains the discrepancy between open-ended solving and concept recognition. Existing category analyses, cross-task comparisons, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The stated repeated-run policy, averaging, per-attempt reporting, and judge-agreement validation are unchanged. v4 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 14 reports the separate-image control results, including GPT-4o's Task-1-only count of 12 versus 13 under composite presentation. Section 5 corrects the especially-hard-problem count from 13 to 10, already reported in v2's appendix and Figure 11. Existing benchmark table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions and Type I–IV behavioral categories are unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, four-part contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims about VLM shortcomings, human comparison, and inconsistent performance across reasoning tasks.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new presentation control as evidence that composite-image presentation does not explain the cross-task discrepancy. The broader perception-versus-reasoning discussion and limitations concerning narrow coverage, training contamination, and LLM judging remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 provides limited reproducibility information for the new control: twelve separate images and changes confined to the prompt's image introduction. Existing model versions, hyperparameters, hardware, prompt listings, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 replace the description of Małkiński et al. as classification-only with acknowledgment of their open-ended evaluation. v4 instead distinguishes its additional diagnostic tasks and focus on original Bongard problems. Other citation changes primarily update metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: v4 organizes Appendix B into task-specific subsections, reformats the research questions, refines several explanatory paragraphs, and corrects cross-references. Author and publication-header text also changes, while most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 14, regroups and renumbers appendix tables, relocates several figures, and standardizes model labels. Figure 4's solved-status legend is revised. The existing figures and table designs otherwise remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: The two-model presentation control modestly strengthens the diagnosis by testing an alternative explanation for cross-task discrepancies. Corrected prior-work positioning, the consistent hard-problem count, and clearer appendix organization also improve accuracy and usability. The main empirical evidence and acknowledged limitations remain largely unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
